speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis (likely Gonococcal) with reactive arthritis history. The 17-year-old male presents with acute monoarticular wrist pain, fever, chills, and malaise following a self-resolving knee episode, all suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI). His recent camping trip in Minnesota is a distractor. Immediate synovial fluid analysis and blood cultures are required. REQUEST TEST: Synovial_Fluid_Analysis, Blood_Culture, Syphilis_Serology, HIV_Antibody_Test. REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist_X-Ray.
